The divergence source is a draw-count or roll-phase difference not yet located, not a movement rule.

The phone's per-cycle press timings are in the frame trace (mask luma, monitor luma, the white static frame at cameras-up), and they differ from the schedule by more than the g378/g379 margin. The seed search must be re-run with the OBSERVED per-cycle press times (mask on/off, monitor up/down) fed to the model instead of the schedule, on full-06, full-04 and full-02.

pressAlignmentFull06.traceColumns: mask_downstroke / monitor_downstroke are the two bottom buttons (actuation-frame-metric.py: both visible = office, mask absent + monitor visible = cameras up); grid row 4 cells show the mask sprite, the hall flash and the camera-up static frame
pressAlignmentFull06.reading: every press, hold or tap, takes effect 212-220 ms after its scheduled time, identically in all three cycles: a uniform latency, i.e. the true epoch for full-06 is ~2580 ms (2364 + 216), not a tap-on-release rule. A taps-on-release variant was tried and kills the model at 20 s (the hall flash falls inside the mask take-off; the dump's g84 needs mask value0 == 0), so it is wrong. In game time the hall flash lands on the roll frame itself (109.98-110.00 s in cycle 10): the k3 flash sits on the 5 s roll by design (hallOffsetMs 7400), a razor edge the phone resolves per cycle.

censusFull06Aligned.setup: all 65,536 seeds on full-06 at the press-aligned epoch 2564 ms (first office frame 198), per-frame trace clock, reference options plus sourcedRandomImageDraw
censusFull06Aligned.reading: With the epoch fixed from the trace instead of fitted, the bracket candidate 47598 ranks 15th of 65,536 by whole-night fit (top 0.02%); the chance that one of 14 bracket seeds lands in the top 15 is about 0.3%. It is the sharpest seed signal of the three nights, and it appears only under the press-aligned epoch and the random-image draw. It is not a lock: 14 seeds fit better, the best still conflicts on 4 cycles, and 47598's exact prefix is 2 (its early cycles conflict while its later ones match, which points at an opening-phase model error rather than the loop).
censusFull06Aligned.verdict: NO LOCK by the predeclared rule (0 conflicts). Candidate: 47598 at 0.3% chance level. Next: the opening-phase presses (cycles 0-4) aligned from the trace the same way, then repeat on full-04 and full-02 with their own trace-fixed epochs.

observedPressesFull06.harness: seedlock-obs.mjs: cfg.cycleEpochs[c] replaces the constant epoch for loop c (observed presses)
observedPressesFull06.result: 14 window seeds x 300 controls x 7 first frames, reference and random-image options: ALL 2,198 runs die (0 alive). Deaths cluster at 60 s (13%), 160 s, 180 s (Foxy, g571/g572 10 s kill after g390 put him at marker 123) and 27-35 s (Toy Bonnie: inside at the 30.17 s camera raise via g546, being attacked = 5 at the 33.86 s monitor lowering via g568, killed 0.67 s later; the route's mask tap follows at 34.31 s). The phone won this night with these exact timings.
observedPressesFull06.dumpForToyBonnie: g568: new bonnie at 123 + being attacked == 0 + mmonitorDown.Active (-29) -> being attacked = 5; g722: at 123 + viewing > 0 + every 10 s -> 5. No mask escape exists once 136 > 0 (g624 forces everything down). So on the phone Toy Bonnie was NOT at marker 123 when the monitor came down: the model's vent-to-office transition (g546 / entryGate camsDown / vent light) or his stun clock is wrong at the true timing.
observedPressesFull06.dumpForFoxy: g389/g390 advance Foxy on a passed roll only while viewing hall light == 0; g489 sets it on any loop with lit? == 1 and viewing == 0, g488 clears it every 1 s. The phone's 33 ms flash straddles the roll frame (109.98-110.00 s in cycle 10) and Foxy never reached 123 in 42 cycles; the model at the same timings lets him through in 13% of runs at 60 s. The latch/flash ordering at the roll frame is the suspect (press and release applied at frame midpoints; g389 evaluated before g488 in the sheet).
observedPressesFull06.consequence: The k3 route as the phone actually executes it is lethal in the model and safe on the phone. The nominal-schedule scoring that made the model survive did so by pressing 200 ms early. Until the Toy Bonnie vent/office transition and the flash-on-roll latch match the phone under observed presses, no seed score means anything, and the route model itself is wrong where it matters (Night 7 deaths).
observedPressesFull06.verdict: NO LOCK. Two model defects isolated with reproducers (probe-tb-obs.mjs seed 47598 first 200 22-34.7 s; probe-foxy-obs.mjs). These outrank the seed search.
